*To the King
Even as I write the bombs still drop. The land and streets we once fought and died to save are being swatted at by our own hands. Innocents are shot down in the same lines as the criminals. The soldiers here harass and slaughter civilians all the while crying out "Bully for me, another one down, hail to the king." As I write the people are still dying, my tears streaming down on the paper. How will the people of this land ever come to sing "God save the King" if the crown is shown to be their demise. The shame I have felt for flying our proud flag has caused my to hide it from this abhorrent and reckless destruction. This night will be remembered by the rebels not as a deterrent from fighting but as a call to action, and from the ashes more will come, and the fighting will continue, and the death till will rise for us all. I beg of you to order a stop to this slaughter in your name, before the damage is irreparable. I beg of you

Former CPT Johnathan Wrask*

“Hello survivors of Empire City. If you’re hearing this, it means you have found somewhere to lie low, or you found yourself in a jail cell. Today is a sad day.

We were bested. Out gunned, outmanned, outnumbered and outplanned. We lost this battle, but the heart of the city perseveres for the war. Do not get caught outside. Regroup at the moorage or with whomever you can find.

Tomorrow we will strike back and bury these redcoats that were so quick to overwhelm us. Stay whelmed and do Not back down.

Now that we see where we were beaten, let us see what inspires hope. We did Not let them storm in and take our city. We fought them at every turn. Engagements broke out at the docks, the sewers, the streets, and in the Noir trying to keep back this incursion.

At the docks I personally witnessed a group of heroes try to keep friends from being taken. Three of us escaped with our lives and lived to fight on again in the streets.

If you have a god, pray to it, if you don’t then let us lend our spirits to one another. We shall not break, we shall not bend. No More!

I’ll see you all tomorrow. Look to the skies for your arms, and let freedom ring. This is your host Finn Midask with the truth, Signing off.”
